title: A file literally named "-rf" is not a filename to most command-line tools; it is two flags
assumption: A string you pass as a filename argument is always interpreted as a filename.

input.description: A filename generated from user content (a title, a hashtag, a ticket id) that happens to start with a hyphen, then passed as a bare positional argument to a CLI tool or argument parser.

what_goes_wrong: A command built as `tool <filename>` with a filename of "-rf" is read by the tool's argument parser as options, not a filename. At best the tool errors out; in the classic case, `rm *` in a directory containing a file named "-rf" hands that name to rm as an argument, and GNU rm (which accepts options anywhere on the command line) reads it as its own -r and -f flags, so rm deletes the other matched directories recursively and without prompting.
why: POSIX-style argument parsers decide whether a token is an option by its first character: a leading '-' (other than a lone "-", which conventionally means standard input) marks it as a flag, whatever the program meant that argument to be. Python's argparse applies this rule and refuses "-rf" as a positional, exiting with a usage error. Node's util.parseArgs, in its non-strict mode, silently parses it as the two boolean flags r and f and leaves no positional at all; in strict mode it throws on the unknown option. Both accept the same token as a filename once it follows a "--" end-of-options marker.
affects: posix-style cli argument parsing (not limited to one language)
node util.parseArgs (non-strict: parses it as flags; strict: throws)

repros.code:
import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("filename")
try:
    args = parser.parse_args(["-rf"])
    print("parsed filename:", args.filename)
except SystemExit as e:
    print("argparse rejected it as a flag, exit code", e.code)
repros.expected_output: argparse rejected it as a flag, exit code 2

fix: When a value could plausibly start with '-', pass it after a literal `--` end-of-options marker wherever the tool supports one, or prefix it with `./` so it no longer starts with a dash.

sources.title: POSIX: Utility Syntax Guidelines (Guideline 10, the -- delimiter)
GNU C Library: Program Argument Syntax Conventions

test_cases.note: A generated filename that starts with '-' needs an explicit escape before it reaches a CLI argument list, or it won't be read as a filename at all.
